title: Molt links tools into dev checkouts against hv's 27 Oct rule: pplr always, utilz by default when a sleeve names no source
body:
## What

hv ruled on 27 Oct 2026, in utilz-vc's session and relayed verbatim by utilz-vc to molt-vc after its removal of `~/.config/menuz/bin/arngz` at 09:53:24Z: "that should be true of all of the ~/bin/* links that are linked to a hardcoded dev install location, rather than using whatever use has set up." That link had pointed the menu at Utilz's dev checkout whatever `utilz use` said.

Molt makes links of this kind itself:

- The pplr liberator always links `$MOLT_LOCAL_BIN/pplr` to `$MOLT_PPLR_HOME/bin/pplr`, the Pplr dev checkout (`liberators/pplr.sh:45`). On rhadamanth that is `~/.local/bin/pplr -> ~/Devel/prj/Pplr/bin/pplr`, and the liberator is enabled there.
- The utilz liberator's checkout mode links `$MOLT_LOCAL_BIN/utilz` and every utility to the Utilz checkout (`liberators/utilz.sh:172` and `:178`). Checkout is the DEFAULT when a sleeve's manifest names no `source` (`_utilz_source`, `liberators/utilz.sh:26`). rhadamanth's manifest says `source = "brew"`, so nothing is linked there, but any sleeve that leaves the line out gets dev links that bypass `utilz use`.

## Measured

molt-vc read `ls -la ~/.local/bin` on rhadamanth on 27 Oct. The links into `~/Devel` were `cdtempl`, `conflab` and `conflabd`, `gtools`, `intent` and `intentd`, `pplr`, and `web`. Only `pplr` and `web` are Molt's. `web` points at `~/Devel/opt/web/web`, an opt build, not a dev checkout. The others belong to their own tools, and their owners answer for them. Gtools and Intent each have a `use` of their own, which molt-vc did not check against these links.

## Next

1. The utilz liberator never links into the checkout: brew is the default, and dev or opt come only from `utilz use`.
2. pplr has no Homebrew formula and no `use`, so its link is its only install. hv decides the target: a pplr formula, a `use` for pplr, or an opt install that the link may name.
3. A check names any link Molt finds pointing into a dev checkout and gives the tool's own `use` as the remedy, without changing the link itself (decision 18: doctors name a stray dev or opt switch, never flip it).

Molt's builders start only when hv calls Molt.
